heading: Los Angeles USCIS medical exam choice: speed claims versus full-process clarity
i693_document_requirements: Form I-693 itself, in the edition USCIS currently accepts. Confirm the edition with the office before the appointment.

Government-issued photo identification such as a valid passport or driver's licence. USCIS sets a different rule for applicants aged 14 or younger: identification showing name, date and place of birth, and a parent's full name — a birth certificate with an English translation, or an affidavit.

A record of your vaccinations or immunisations. USCIS names the ones it means: DT, DTP, DTaP, Td, Tdap, OPV, IPV, MMR, Hib, Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B, Varicella, Pneumococcal, Influenza, Rotavirus and Meningococcal disease.
Your health insurance card, with the question already prepared: does this office accept the plan for immigration medical examinations?
Payment, in a form the office has told you it accepts.
If you have ever had a positive tuberculosis test or treatment, bring the chest X-ray report or treatment records; it can save a repeat X-ray.
Do not sign Form I-693 before the visit. You sign it in front of the civil surgeon.
vaccination_handling_notes: If you were vaccinated in California, your record may be in CAIR, the California Immunization Registry run by the California Department of Public Health. Ask the clinic or school that vaccinated you to print it from CAIR before the exam.
Arriving with the records is the cheapest thing you can do. Without them the choice is repeat doses or blood tests to prove immunity, and both cost money and time.
In Los Angeles, the useful question is whether missing vaccines can be solved through the same clinic workflow.
bilingual_support: If language support matters, confirm it covers instructions and form review, not just front-desk scheduling.
appointment_booking_notes: Ask the clinic to describe booking, exam, tests, vaccines, and packet release in a single timeline.
Booking flow: verify USCIS designation, ask total cost, confirm documents/vaccine records, schedule exam, complete labs/vaccines, then pick up sealed packet after final review.
